'''Harald J.W. Mueller-Kirsten''' (born 1935) is a German theoretical physicist specializing in [[theoretical particle physics]] and [[mathematical physics]].

==Education and career==
Müller-Kirsten obtained the B.Sc. (First Class Honours) in 1957 and the Ph.D. in 1960 from the [[University of Western Australia]] in Perth, where his [[doctoral advisor]] was [[Robert Balson Dingle]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.rse.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/obits_alpha/dingle_robert.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=2020-07-01 |archive-date=2017-12-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171222220035/https://www.rse.org.uk/cms/files/fellows/obits_alpha/dingle_robert.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Thereafter he was postdoc at [[LMU Munich]] (Institute of [[F. Bopp]]) and obtained the [[habilitation]] there in 1971.  Müller-Kirsten was an assistant professor at the [[American University of Beirut]] in 1967, NATO-Fellow at the Lawrence Radiation Laboratory in Berkeley in 1970, and Max-Kade-Foundation Fellow at SLAC, Stanford in 1974–75.  In 1972, he was appointed Wissenschaftlicher Rat and Professor (H2) at the [[University of Kaiserslautern]], then there in 1976 University Professor (C2) and in 1995 University Professor (C3).

==Research achievements==
# [[Asymptotic expansions]] of [[Mathieu function]]s, [[spheroidal wave function]]s, [[Lamé function]]s and ellipsoidal wave functions and their eigenvalues.<ref>R.B. Dingle and H.J.W. Müller, J. reine angew. Math. 211 (1962) 11–32, 216 (1964) 123–133; H.J.W. Müller, J. reine angew. Math. 211 (1962) 33.47, 211 (1962) 179–190, 212 (1963) 26–48; H.J.W. Müller, Math. Nachr. 31 (1966) 89–101, 32 (1966) 49–62, 32 (1966) 157–374.</ref>
# [[Asymptotic expansions]] of Regge poles for [[Yukawa potential]]s (in agreement with [[Langer]]-corrected WKB calculations).<ref>H.J.W. Müller, Ann. d. Phys. (Leipzig) 15 (1965) 395–411.; H.J.W. Müller and K. Schilcher, J. Math. Phys. 9 (1968) 255–259.</ref>
# Eigenvalue and level-splitting formula for [[double-well potential]]s.<ref>H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten, Introduction to Quantum Mechanics: Schrödinger Equation and Path Integral, World Scientific Singapore, 2nd ed., 2012, {{ISBN|978-981-4397-73-5}}, pp. 524–527; J.-Q. Liang and H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten, Anharmonic Oscillator Equations: Treatment Parallel to Mathieu Equation, quant-ph/0407235; P. Achuthan, H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten and A. Wiedemann, Fortschr. Physik 38 (1990) 77.</ref>
# [[Line integral|Path integral]] method applied to quartic and cosine potentials.<ref>J.-Q. Liang and H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten, Phys. Rev. D46 (1992) 4685, D50 (1994) 6519, D51 (1995) 718.</ref>
# Discovery that for quartic and cosine potentials the equation of small fluctuations around the classical solution is a [[Lamé equation]].<ref>J.-Q. Liang, H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten and D.H. Tchrakian, Phys. Lett. B282 (1992) 105.</ref>
# Derivation of [[S-matrix]] and absorptivity for the singular potential <math>1/r^4</math> (cf. modified Mathieu equation) and application to [[string theory]].<ref>H.H. Aly, H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten and N. Vahedi-Faridi, J. Math. Phys. 16 (1975) 961; R. Manvelyan, H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten, J.-Q. Liang and Yunbo Zhang, Nucl. Phys. B579 (2000) 177, hep-th/0001179; D.K. Park, S.N. Tamaryan, H.J.W. Müller-Kirsten and Jian-Zu Zhang, Nucl. Phys. B594 (2001) 243, hep-th/0005165.</ref>
# Construction and [[quantization (physics)|quantization]] of [[gauge theory]] models,<ref>[[Usha Kulshreshtha]], [[Daya Shankar Kulshreshtha]], Harald J.W. Mueller-Kirsten, `'A Gauge invariant theory of chiral bosons: Wess–Zumino term, Hamiltonian and BRST formulations'`, Zeit. Phys. C 60 (1993) 427–431.</ref> Faddeev–Jackiw quantization of systems with constraints,<ref>[[Daya Shankar Kulshreshtha]], Harald J.W. Mueller-Kirsten, `'Quantization of systems with constraints: The Faddeev–Jackiw method versus Dirac's method applied to superfields'`, Phys. Rev. D43 (1991) 3376–3383; `'Faddeev-Jackiw quantization of selfdual fields'`, Phys. Rev. D 45 (1992) 393–397.</ref>
